transcript: Sahana bhavato sahano bhunakto sahaviryam karavavahai te Jasvinavadhitamastuma vidvishavahai Om Shanti Shanti Shanti Om Yam Brahma Varunendra Rudra anti devyastavaih vedaih sangapadakramopanishadaih gayanti samsaragah dhyanavati Sthita yasyam tam na vidu surasuraganah devayat devayat So in the first chapter, Arjuna gives all the reasons why they should not fight the war. I think it is better to beg and live than kill these noble ones. But then Arjuna himself realizes that there is a deep confusion within. What is dharma, what is adharma, what is right, what is wrong, what should be done, what should not be done. He realizes his confusion, but one great thing Arjuna does is, he completely surrenders unto Bhagwan. The first chapter is called Arjuna Vishada Yoga. Now a question may come, how can Vishada be considered Yoga? Vishada means sorrow. Yoga is a science of uniting with the Lord. How can sorrow be considered a yoga? But then the answer given is, it is because of this sorrow that Arjuna surrendered unto Bhagwan. It is because of this sorrow that Arjuna sought this greatest knowledge. So therefore, even this sorrow, is a blessing in disguise. Even this sorrow is an auspicious beginning. It is not inauspicious, though superficially it may appear to be inauspicious. So even this vishada is considered to be yoga because vishada opens up the door. towards yoga. So then Arjuna surrenders completely to Bhagwan, saying Bhagwan, I am absolutely helpless. Though I have all the talents and abilities to fight the war, but these talents I am not able to bring it out. because of utter helplessness, born out of confusion regarding what is dharma and what is adharma. So therefore Bhagwan, nishchitam shreyah, whatever it is, please tell me. Whatever is ultimately good for me, ultimately good for all. For all times, whatever it is, please tell me, please guide me.
